title: Efficacy and Safety of Intraosseous Regional Versus Intravenous Tranexamic Acid in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces perioperative blood loss in total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, evidence for intraosseous regional administration (IORA) remains limited. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of IORA-TXA versus intravenous TXA (IV-TXA) in TKA. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg. The primary outcome was calculated perioperative blood loss. Secondary efficacy outcomes included calculated hidden blood loss, postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and transfusion rate. Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular calf vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and wound-related complications. RESULTS: Compared with IV-TXA, IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative blood loss (674.8 ± 335.0 vs. 817.5 ± 357.2 mL; mean difference, 142.6 mL; 95% CI, 7.4-277.8; p = 0.038) and calculated hidden blood loss (644.8 ± 335.5 vs. 790.9 ± 339.0 mL; mean difference, 146.1 mL; 95% CI, 10.9-281.3; p = 0.035). Postoperative Hb was similar on POD1 (134.0 ± 9.8 vs. 130.1 ± 11.1 g/L; p = 0.067) but was higher with IORA-TXA on POD2 (119.8 ± 8.3 vs. 113.8 ± 11.5 g/L; mean difference 6.0 g/L; 95% CI 2.0-10.0; p = 0.005) and POD3 (114.8 ± 7.9 vs. 109.8 ± 12.6 g/L; mean difference 5.0 g/L; 95% CI 0.8-9.2; p = 0.020). No patient required blood transfusion. DVT detected by routine postoperative Doppler occurred numerically more often with IORA-TXA than with IV-TXA: 10.2% (95% CI, 3.4%-22.2%) versus 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0%-7.3%); p = 0.056. CONCLUSIONS: IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative and hidden blood loss and improved early postoperative Hb preservation compared with IV-TXA. However, DVT incidence was numerically higher with IORA-TXA, indicating a potential thromboembolic safety signal that warrants confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg.

title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
abstract: Background: Patients and methods: Results: Conclusions Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes.We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex.Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing.: Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

title: Long-Term Quantitative MRI and Quality-of-Life After Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke - A MR CLEAN-NO IV Substudy.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 This study aims to explore the long-term evolution of endovascular treatment after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) using quantitative MRI, and its relationship with quality of life (QoL). In this long-term substudy of patients from the MR CLEAN-NO IV trial, patients were included who received 24-hour post-stroke MRI and were functionally independent 90 days after stroke onset. Patients underwent a quantitative MRI exam three years after stroke onset to measure focal volume loss, myelin damage, iron deposition, and atrophy within and around the ischemic lesion seen on 24-hour-MRI, in addition to a QoL assessment. Bayesian statistical analyses were used to assess MRI measures lateralized to the ipsilateral hemisphere and to evaluate the relationship of these measures with baseline and treatment characteristics along with QoL. The Bayes Factor (BF) reflected moderate, strong or very strong evidence (BF = 3.0;20;1.5⋅10respectively). In the 24 included patients, prominent focal volume loss, iron deposition, ventricular enlargement and myelin damage (BF:2.0⋅10) were observed peripheral to the initial 24-hour DWI lesion at long-term FU MRI. In the basal ganglia nuclei, very strong evidence of focal volume loss (BF > 8.1⋅10) and moderate to very strong evidence of iron deposition (BF: 5.0 to 2.7⋅10) were observed at long-term assessment. Higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced long-term ventricular atrophy (BF:5.8). Long-term differences in ipsilateral versus contralateral hippocampal volume difference (BF:8.0) and iron deposition (BF:4.1) were moderately associated with QoL. Long-term subtle yet widespread demyelination and iron deposition were observed, and these changes correlated with long-term recovery.

title: [Chinese guideline for the laboratory diagnosis of venous thromboembolism (2026 edition)].
abstract: Chinese guideline for the laboratory diagnosis of venous thromboembolism 2026 edition Guiding Principles for the Formulation and Revision of Clinical Practice Guidelines in China (2022 Edition) Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a multifactorial disease induced by the interplay between environmental exposures and genetic predisposition. It features intricate pathological mechanisms and an insidious clinical course, with severe cases potentially resulting in disability or death. In recent years, laboratory assays for VTE have become increasingly diverse,nevertheless, prominent challenges persist, including ambiguous indications for clinical application, inconsistent interpretation criteria, and insufficient evidence-based support. To further promote the standardization of laboratory diagnosis for VTE in China, enhance the safety and efficacy of clinical applications, and ensure the rational utilization of diagnostic resources, initiated by Expert Committee of the National Capacity Building Project for Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Venous Thrombosis Prevention and Treatment, National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and National Center for Clinical Laboratories, the() was developed in accordance with the methodologies and procedures in the, the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation Ⅱ (AGREEⅡ), and the Reporting Items for Practice Guidelines in Healthcare (RIGHT). This guideline addresses 12 clinical questions and includes 33 recommendations, covering exclusion diagnosis, etiological analysis, risk assessment and anticoagulation monitoring of VTE. It is intended to establish a VTE laboratory testing system adapted to domestic conditions in China, so as to promote standardization and homogenization of VTE laboratory diagnosis.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Beyond Patency: Patient-Centered Outcomes and the Proposed Accountability Gap in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries 1-year mortality of 20% to 25%, comparable with many solid-organ malignancies. Technically successful revascularization, defined by anatomical patency, does not reliably deliver pain relief, restored function, or sustained quality of life. This narrative review synthesizes landmark randomized trials (BEST-CLI, BASIL-1, BASIL-2) and current European and United States guidelines, grading every claim with a scheme in which population indirectness downgrades design strength. We examine 4 domains of morbidity persisting after anatomically successful revascularization: mechanistically heterogeneous pain; functional and quality-of-life decline; psychological burden; and sustained health care use, including chronic opioid use (approximately 35%), unhealed wounds at 1 year (10%-32%), and unplanned 30-day readmission (approximately 25%). No patient-reported outcome measure has been validated specifically for CLTI or used as a co-primary trial endpoint. We propose an accountability gap: the under-measured transfer of unresolved morbidity from vascular services to primary care. We state it as a falsifiable prediction about the discrimination of patency rather than prevalence, with a pre-specified effect size, explicit treatment of death as a competing risk, and a core outcome battery justified against COSMIN criteria. Patient co-production is the indispensable next step.

title: Comparison of different interventions for promoting the maturation of autogenous arteriovenous fistula: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred access for patients undergoing hemodialysis. This study sought to identify the optimal intervention for promoting the maturation of AVFs through a network meta-analysis (NMA). METHODS: Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science databases were searched by computer for publications up to May 12, 2025, utilizing primary terms such as "arteriovenous fistula" and "maturation." Risk of bias was assessed utilizing the tool from the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews. Funnel plots and Egger's test were used to assess publication bias. Primary outcomes were the ultrasonographic and clinical maturation of AVFs. The secondary outcome was the vein diameter. An NMA was conducted employing a Bayesian random-effects or fixed-effects model. Mean differences (MD) and relative risks (RR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI) were calculated. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were utilized to rank different interventions. Analyses were performed using R 4.3.2. RESULTS: Finally, 11 RCTs involving 1202 patients were included. The studies encompassed a total of 5 interventions, namely isometric exercise (ISOM), isotonic exercise (ISOT), ISOM+ISOT, far infrared (FIR) therapy, and balloon-assisted maturation (BAM). The NMA revealed that compared with conventional care, ISOM ranked first in improving clinical maturation (RR = 1.4, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.7, SUCRA = 98.07%) and ultrasonographic maturation (RR = 1.5, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.8, SUCRA = 99.88%). ISOM+ISOT ranked first in increasing the diameter of the outflow vein (MD = 0.84, 95% CrI: 0.68, 1.0, SUCRA = 87.24%). CONCLUSION: n This study suggests that, among the evaluated interventions, ISOM has the highest probability of improving clinical maturation of AVFs based on moderate-certainty evidence, and evidence supporting its effect on ultrasonographic maturation is tentative given the limited sample size ( = 340). ISOM + ISOT demonstrated the greatest likelihood of effectively increasing vein diameter. These findings are probabilistic and require individualized application.

title: Preoperative levels of biomarkers of coagulation to predict massive bleeding after surgical repair for acute type A aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly emergent condition with a high mortality rate. The condition poses an imminent risk of serious complications such as coagulopathy with massive bleeding. This increases the risk of mortality even after surgical repair. Procoagulant drugs are routinely administered but some patients still suffer postoperative massive bleeding that can be fatal. The study aimed to investigate whether massive bleeding after surgical treatment for type A aortic dissection can be predicted preoperatively through routine coagulation tests such as APTT, PT (INR), fibrinogen, D-dimer, and platelets. METHODS: The study was a retrospective, single-center, cohort study performed at a tertiary cardiac surgery unit. A total of 474 patients who underwent surgery for type A aortic dissection at our department between January 2005 and May 2023 were included in the study. Of these, 87 patients had massive postoperative bleeding after surgery for type A aortic dissection and were compared to 387 patients who did not have massive postoperative bleeding. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed using logistic regression. The multivariable model included predictors of massive bleeding. Bleeding-related routine lab variables were then forced into the model. RESULTS: 9 9 Patients with massive bleeding (18%) had higher preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) (33 s vs 29 s, p<0.01), and creatinine (97 µmol/L vs 87 µmol/L, p<0.01), as well as lower preoperative platelet counts (172 × 10/L vs 187 × 10/L, p=0.03) compared to patients without massive bleeding. Patients with massive bleeding also had longer duration of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) (221 min vs 170 min, p<0.01) and suffered more postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative APTT per mmol increment (OR 1.04 (95% CI 1.01-1.07, p=0.01), preoperative APTT > 34.5 s (OR 2.95 (95% CI 1.60-5.47), p<0.01), preoperative creatinine > 82.5 µmol/L (OR 2.16 (95% CI 1.15-4.06), p=0.02), hypertension (OR 1.83 (95% CI 1.01-3.32), p<0.05) and CPB time per 10 min increment (OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13, p<0.01)) as independent predictors of massive bleeding. CONCLUSION: Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

title: [Varicocele: comparison of minimally invasive treatment options : Endovascular embolization, microsurgery, and patient-tailored treatment selection].
abstract: BACKGROUND: Varicocele is the most common potentially treatable cause of male subfertility. Endovascular embolization is an established minimally invasive alternative to microsurgical ligation. OBJECTIVE: To place the indications, technique, outcomes, and limitations of varicocele embolization in context and to define its role relative to microsurgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative, guideline- and evidence-based review of current WHO, EAU, AUA/ASRM, and CIRSE recommendations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant cohort studies published through July 2026. RESULTS: Treatment is primarily indicated in men with a palpable varicocele, abnormal semen parameters, and otherwise unexplained infertility; subclinical varicoceles and normal semen analyses do not justify intervention. Technical success of embolization is usually above 90% in experienced centers. Pregnancy rates are broadly similar to those after surgery, while overall morbidity tends to be lower. Recurrence may, however, be more frequent than after high ligation. No embolic agent has proved consistently superior. CONCLUSION: Varicocele embolization is an evidence-based alternative to surgery, particularly for recurrent disease, bilateral or complex venous anatomy, and when rapid recovery is a priority. Treatment should be selected through multidisciplinary, anatomy-based, and shared decision-making.

Endovascular embolization is an established minimally invasive alternative to microsurgical ligation. title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I= 0%; t= 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I= 0%; t= 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I= 0%; τ= 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1). METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions. METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years. RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used. CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1. CONCLUSION: CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

title: Cerebral No-Reflow after Thrombectomy: International Delphi Consensus on Definition and Imaging Assessment.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The operational definition and imaging assessment of the no-reflow phenomenon, a potential contributor to poor clinical outcome despite successful thrombectomy, remains debated. We aimed to develop expert-based international consensus on the definition, assessment, and reporting standard of cerebral no-reflow post-thrombectomy. METHODS: Three-rounds of a modified Delphi web-based survey was conducted among corresponding authors of peer-reviewed clinical studies on cerebral no-reflow between 2020 and 2025. Responses at each round were used to develop structured questionnaires for subsequent rounds. Consensus was predefined as ≥65% agreement. RESULTS: Among 27 panelists, the response rate was 70%, 74%, and 74% over all rounds. There was broad agreement to conceptualize no-reflow as macrovascular recanalization with impaired microvascular reperfusion. Consensus was reached that macrovascular recanalization is ideally assessed as (1) digital subtraction angiography with expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) grades 2c without clear distal vessel occlusions and/or eTICI 3 only, and (2) absence of a wedge-shaped time-to-maximum (Tmax) or time-to-peak (TTP) delay on post-recanalization perfusion computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Regarding impaired microvascular reperfusion assessment, cerebral blood flow, and/or volume were preferred over time-based perfusion parameters (Tmax/TTP). The panel expressed a preference that no-reflow should ideally be assessed ≤6 hours post-recanalization. Pending formal validation, histopathological-radiological correlation in animal models would sufficiently validate the use of imaging-based definitions in humans. INTERPRETATION: Based on currently available literature and expert opinions, this Delphi study provides a framework for systematically reporting cerebral no-reflow after endovascular treatment (EVT). The variability in opinions regarding quantitative thresholds highlights priorities for future methodological standardization and validation studies. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Cardiometabolic Assessment in Patients with Overweight, Obesity, or Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing Artificial Intelligence-Based Retinal Screening: A Real-World Evidence Study.
abstract: Background: Methods: n n n Results: P P P P P Conclusions: Overweight, obesity, and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) increase the risk of vascular complications, including retinal vascular alterations. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based retinal screening enables early detection of microvascular damage, potentially contributing to appropriate cardiometabolic prevention strategies. title: Transforming value-based deep vein thrombosis care through a pharmacist-led clinic.
abstract: PURPOSE: To address gaps in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) care, our health system implemented a pharmacist-led DVT clinic to standardize treatment, provide immediate access to pharmacy and vascular surgery services, and reduce emergency department (ED) and inpatient utilization for DVT management. METHODS: This was a retrospective, pre-post cohort study of a DVT clinic that centralized imaging, diagnosis, anticoagulant initiation, and pharmacy services into a single outpatient location. Patients diagnosed with a DVT between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, were included. The co-primary outcomes were the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the acute care setting compared before and after the DVT clinic opened (2023 vs 2024) and compared between patients seen in the clinic or not (2024 only). A χ2 test was used to analyze the co-primary outcomes, with significance defined as a P value of less than 0.05. RESULTS: The pharmacist saw 205 patients across 363 visits in 2024. Compared to 2023 baseline data, the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the ED in 2024 decreased from 88.6% to 53.3% (P < 0.001), while the rate of inpatient admission for DVT decreased from 25.5% to 13.9% (P < 0.001). Stratified analysis of the 2024 data demonstrated significantly lower acute care utilization for DVT among patients managed in the DVT clinic compared to those not seen, including for ED encounters (15.2% vs 91.5%; P < 0.001) and inpatient admissions (1.8% vs 26%; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The pharmacist-led DVT clinic represents a transformative advancement in pharmacy practice, redefining the role of pharmacists in ambulatory care and establishing a replicable model to optimize value-based care that shifts treatment for appropriate populations from acute to outpatient management.

title: Venous thromboembolism after laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy with large myoma burden.
abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing myomectomy. To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) SETTING: NSQIP Database PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Women aged ≥18 years undergoing laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy between 2011 and 2022. Patients were classified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes as having low or high myoma burden (>250 g or >4 fibroids). Patients undergoing hysterectomy, vaginal or hysteroscopic myomectomy, with malignant pathology, or missing operative time were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Cases were identified by CPT codes. Variables including age, ethnicity, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, hypertension, blood transfusion, inpatient status, and American Society of Anesthesiologists classification system scores were collected. Clinical predictors of VTE were evaluated by stratifying cases according to surgical route, operative time, year of procedure, and myoma burden. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 38,167 myomectomies occurring between 2011-2022 were included. Of these, 20,943 (54.9%) patients underwent laparotomy, and 17,224 (45.1%) patients underwent laparoscopy. The incidence of VTE after myomectomy was 0.28%. Patients undergoing laparotomy had twice the VTE rate (0.36%) compared with those undergoing laparoscopy (0.18%). Patients undergoing laparotomy were more likely to be younger, of non-Hispanic African American ethnicity, inpatient, with higher BMI, require blood transfusion, have higher myoma burden, and have shorter operative times. After multivariable adjustment, neither myoma burden nor surgical route was independently associated with VTE. However, longer operative time (>186 min, 75 percentile) was independently associated with increased odds of VTE (aOR 2.73; CI:1.52-4.90). CONCLUSION: The occurrence of VTE after laparoscopic and laparotomic myomectomy is uncommon. The rate of VTE is higher with longer operative times, but this outcome is not significantly associated with surgical route or myoma burden.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. RESULTS: P Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89];=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: COG5 Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and aVariant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: HLA-A HLA-DQA2 COG5 TPM4 Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 nearand rs9276409 within) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in thegene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: COG5 This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidatevariant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Optimizing management strategies for T4b esophageal cancer: the role of TEVAR in multimodal treatment approaches.
abstract: BACKGROUND: T4b esophageal cancer with aortic invasion remains a major therapeutic challenge because treatment-related tumor regression may precipitate aortoesophageal fistula formation and catastrophic hemorrhage. While chemoradiotherapy is the backbone of disease control, the role of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) as prophylaxis or bridge therapy within a multimodal treatment strategy is increasingly recognized. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the use of TEVAR in T4b esophageal cancer. Relevant clinical studies, reviews and guideline documents were evaluated qualitatively, with emphasis on treatment sequencing, bleeding prevention, resectability and oncologic outcomes. RESULTS: Available retrospective studies and systematic reviews suggest that elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of major bleeding complications and facilitate subsequent esophagectomy in selected patients. Elective TEVAR was associated with higher rates of subsequent esophageal resection and fewer complications than salvage TEVAR. Moreover, elective TEVAR followed by esophagectomy, ameliorates significantly patients survival. These findings support the potential role of elective TEVAR within multimodal treatment strategies, although the available evidence remains predominantly retrospective and is subject to selection bias and heterogeneity in patient selection and treatment. CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may represent a useful adjunct in the multimodal management of selected patients with T4b esophageal cancer and aortic involvement. In carefully selected patients, elective TEVAR may reduce the risk of catastrophic hemorrhage and facilitate subsequent curative-intent treatment, including conversion esophagectomy, although prospective evidence defining its optimal indications and timing remains lacking.

title: Development of best practice statements for anticoagulation in advanced kidney disease using the modified Delphi method.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with advanced kidney disease (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) are known to have an increased risk of venous thromboembolic events and increased likelihood of atrial fibrillation alongside an increased risk of bleeding. People with advanced kidney disease are often excluded from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of anticoagulants, leaving gaps in the evidence base and practice variation. This study aimed to achieve consensus on anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease to inform national prescribing guidance. METHODS: A modified Delphi approach was used to achieve consensus on statements relating to anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease. Three Delphi rounds were predefined, with two rounds of questionnaires followed by online discussion in round three. Panel members included UK experts from the fields of cardiology, nephrology and haematology, who were asked to rate 160 statements with appropriateness and consensus defined by RAND methodology. RESULTS: Twenty-one experts completed rounds one and two of the Delphi. For round three, 11 experts joined a Microsoft Teams discussion. Following round three, there were 72 statements with consensus agreement for inclusion in the guideline, including dose reduction recommendations for therapeutic light molecular weight heparin (LMWH), recommendation for off-label apixaban use in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, and trough anti-Xa level monitoring with therapeutic LMWH. Forty-two statements with consensus disagreement for exclusion and 27 with unequivocal consensus. These statements could be used to develop research recommendations. CONCLUSION: This study has led to consensus agreement on a number of statements relating to anticoagulant use in advanced kidney disease in the UK that can be used in national guidance.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.

title: Suspected Mesenteric Malperfusion in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection During Pregnancy: A Case Report and Review of Reperfusion-First Strategies.
abstract: Aortic dissection during pregnancy is rare but potentially catastrophic. Acute Type A aortic dissection generally requires urgent surgical repair. When visceral malperfusion is present, however, the optimal sequence of interventions may be complex, particularly when pregnancy and recent cesarean delivery increase operative risk. Endovascular reperfusion followed by delayed aortic repair has been proposed in selected patients, although evidence supporting this strategy in pregnancy remains limited. A 37-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation presented with chest and back pain. Initial CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) performed for suspected pulmonary embolism excluded pulmonary embolism but demonstrated marked aortic root dilatation measuring 6.7 × 5.4 cm. Before definitive aortic imaging could be obtained, she developed acute respiratory deterioration and fetal distress, prompting emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe aortic root and ascending aortic dilatation, severe aortic regurgitation, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and a dissection flap consistent with Type A aortic dissection. Because of concern for catastrophic hemorrhage associated with cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest shortly after cesarean delivery, definitive aortic repair was deferred for approximately 24 h while the patient underwent medical optimization. During this interval, she developed progressive metabolic acidosis and worsening renal function, raising clinical concern for visceral malperfusion. Dedicated abdominal vascular imaging was not obtained, and therefore the presence, distribution, and mechanism of mesenteric malperfusion could not be anatomically confirmed before surgery. At subsequent operative exploration, extensive small- and large-bowel necrosis and markedly hypoperfused adnexal tissue were identified, precluding definitive aortic repair. The patient subsequently died after transition to comfort-focused care. In an analysis from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection, mesenteric malperfusion was associated with higher in-hospital mortality than dissection without malperfusion. This case highlights the diagnostic and management challenges of acute Type A aortic dissection during pregnancy. In a pregnant patient presenting with chest or back pain and marked aortic root dilatation on PE-protocol imaging, acute aortic syndrome should prompt urgent evaluation of the entire aorta. Progressive metabolic acidosis, renal dysfunction, or unexplained clinical deterioration should raise concern for visceral ischemia. Although reperfusion-first strategies have been described in selected patients with aortic dissection and mesenteric malperfusion, their applicability in pregnancy remains uncertain and depends on defined vascular anatomy and the mechanism of malperfusion.

title: Post-transfer reassessment for endovascular treatment: factors associated with changes in EVT eligibility.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Repeat imaging after interhospital transfer for endovascular treatment (EVT) remains controversial because EVT eligibility may change during transfer, whereas routine repeat imaging may delay reperfusion. We investigated factors associated with complete recanalization and extensive infarct progression, and their implications for post-transfer reassessment. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 200 consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion transferred for EVT between 2016 and 2020 who underwent repeat non-contrast CT, CT angiography, and serial neurological assessment. Primary outcomes were complete recanalization on repeat CT angiography and extensive infarct progression (ASPECTS 0-3) precluding EVT. Factors associated with both outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. RESULTS: Changes affecting EVT eligibility occurred in 19 patients (9.5%), including complete recanalization in 10 (5.0%) and extensive infarct progression in 9 (4.5%). Intravenous thrombolysis was associated with complete recanalization (OR 4.87, 95% CI 1.08-46.25; P = 0.039), while greater neurological improvement showed a consistent direction of association (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18; P = 0.059). Greater neurological deterioration (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.97; P = 0.018) and lower baseline CTA source-image ASPECTS (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.34-0.79; P = 0.001) were associated with extensive infarct progression. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in ten transferred patients experienced clinically meaningful changes affecting EVT eligibility. Neurological reassessment combined with baseline CTA source-image ASPECTS may help identify patients most likely to benefit from repeat imaging and supports a selective rather than routine repeat imaging strategy after interhospital transfer.

title: Apixaban vs rivaroxaban for venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants are first-line therapy for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet comparative evidence between apixaban and rivaroxaban remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in patients with VTE. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 2026. Studies directly comparing apixaban and rivaroxaban in adult VTE patients were included. Outcomes, including recurrent VTE, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, and net clinical harm, were pooled using a random-effects model. Thirteen studies comprising more than 220,000 patients were included. Apixaban was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent VTE compared to rivaroxaban (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.74-0.98), with moderate heterogeneity. Apixaban was also associated with a significant 28% reduction in major bleeding risk (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with low heterogeneity, indicating consistent findings across studies. When efficacy and safety outcomes were combined, apixaban demonstrated a significantly lower risk of net clinical harm (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.68-0.86). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.80-1.12), with substantial heterogeneity across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings, with no single study significantly altering the overall estimates. Overall, apixaban demonstrated a more favorable efficacy and safety profile compared with rivaroxaban in VTE management, with reduced recurrence and bleeding risk, while mortality remained comparable. These findings suggest that apixaban may be associated with a more favorable efficacy and safety profile than rivaroxaban; however, the results should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of observational evidence.

title: Endovascular management of labyrintho-vascular otic capsule dehiscence (type II): A different therapeutical approach.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Otic capsule dehiscence (OCD) encompasses a spectrum of third mobile window disorders, including type II variants characterized by a direct interface between the membranous labyrinth and adjacent vascular structures. These labyrinthine-vascular dehiscences (type IIa: superior semicircular canal-superior petrosal sinus (SPS); type IIb: internal jugular vein-vestibular structures) may induce pulsatile tinnitus, vertigo, and hearing loss. Endovascular treatment has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to conventional surgery, aiming to reduce vascular pulsatility transmission to the inner ear. This study evaluates the interest, clinical outcomes and limitations of such approaches. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series including patients with unilateral type II OCD confirmed by high-resolution imaging and presenting with disabling symptoms as assessed by the DHI and the THI. All patients underwent comprehensive audio-vestibular assessment and multimodal imaging. Endovascular treatment strategies included stenting of the SPS (type IIa) or stent-assisted coiling of the jugular bulb/internal jugular vein (type IIb). Outcomes were assessed clinically, audiometrically, and radiologically at follow-up. RESULTS: Eight patients were included (4 type IIa, 4 type IIb). Endovascular treatment was feasible in most cases, with one technical failure and one conversion to surgery due to unfavorable venous anatomy. At 6 months, 7/7 evaluable patients showed marked clinical improvement, with significant reductions in THI and DHI scores. Pulsatile tinnitus and vertigo improved in the majority of cases. Audiometric outcomes were variable, with closure of the air-bone gap in 4 patients. Vestibular function remained largely preserved, with only transient postoperative impairment in one case. No major complications or venous thrombosis were observed on follow-up imaging. CONCLUSION: Endovascular management of type II OCD appears to be a safe and effective minimally invasive alternative in selected patients, particularly for vascular-related symptoms. The outcomes depend heavily on venous anatomy and meticulous preoperative imaging. While clinical outcomes are encouraging, limitations include technical feasibility and variable auditory results. Endovascular approaches may be considered a first-line option when anatomically suitable, with surgery reserved for selected or failed cases.

title: Microsurgical Resection versus Endovascular Embolization for Intramedullary Spinal Arteriovenous Malformations: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Regression Modeling.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intramedullary spinal arteriovenous malformations (sAVMs) are rare, high-risk lesions associated with progressive neurological decline, ischemia, and hemorrhage. Microsurgical resection (MR) and endovascular embolization (EE) are the primary treatment modalities, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain unclear. PURPOSE: To systematically compare angiographic and clinical outcomes of MR versus EE for intramedullary sAVMs. DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search of PubMed and Embase was performed across major medical databases to identify relevant studies reporting outcomes of MR or EE in intramedullary sAVMs. STUDY SELECTION: Studies including ≥5 patients with intramedullary sAVMs treated with MR or EE and reporting angiographic obliteration and clinical outcomes were included. DATA ANALYSIS: Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled outcome rates. Multivariable mixed-effects meta-regression identified predictors of angiographic and clinical outcomes. DATA SYNTHESIS: Twenty-six studies were included (MR: 193 patients; EE: 303 patients). Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups, although MR patients had slightly higher pain presentation, glomus type lesions, and prior treatment. MR achieved significantly higher complete obliteration rates than EE (80.13% vs 27.44%, p<0.01). There were no significant differences in symptom improvement (42.70% vs 55.52%, p=0.35), complete recovery (36.37% vs 32.58%, p=0.92), worsening (13.81% vs 10.96%, p=0.45), post-treatment hemorrhage (1.83% vs 0.89%, p=0.30), or mortality (1.55% vs 0.99%, p=0.81). Higher obliteration independently predicted symptom improvement, though MR was associated with lower odds of improvement. EE, younger age, and non-hemorrhagic presentation predicted complete recovery. LIMITATIONS: Findings are limited by the retrospective design of included studies, heterogeneity in patient selection and treatment strategies, and potential publication bias. CONCLUSIONS: MR provides higher angiographic obliteration but does not consistently translate to improved clinical recovery, likely due to procedure-related neural injury. EE remains an effective, less invasive option for complex or high-risk lesions, while MR may be best reserved for salvage therapy. Individualized treatment strategies based on lesion characteristics and patient factors are essential.

Microsurgical resection (MR) and endovascular embolization (EE) are the primary treatment modalities, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain unclear. PURPOSE: To systematically compare angiographic and clinical outcomes of MR versus EE for intramedullary sAVMs.

title: Impact of prior antithrombotic therapy on safety and outcomes of endovascular therapy in large-core acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT. RESULTS: interaction interaction A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n = 70; no ATD, n = 132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (p=0.944) or secondary outcomes (p=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

title: Achieving an Endovascular Therapy Door-to-Device Time Under 90 Minutes in Patients with Ischemic Stroke Associates with 90-day mRS.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption. METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke. The likelihood of a favorable patient outcome was quantified for patients with a DTD time ≤90 minutes compared to patients with a DTD time >90 minutes. RESULTS: DTD ≤90 minutes was associated with an increased odds of having a more favorable (0-2) modified Rankin Score at 90-days (AOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-2.00; P = .004) post stroke compared to DTD >90 minutes. We did not find that DTD under or over 90 minutes had a significant association with discharge home (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46; P = .051) or patients' length of stay (β, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.30-0.34; P = .20). CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports that EVT completed with DTD time ≤90 minutes was associated with better functional outcomes for patients.

title: A Comparison of Aspiration Thrombectomy to Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Management of Paget-Schroetter Syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet (Paget Schroetter Syndrome-PSS) may involve prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein by catheter directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive PSS cases at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded by degree of luminal encroachment, and vessel irregularity: mild (less than 10%), moderate (10-50%) and severe (50-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency at last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. 54 met inclusion criteria: 28 CDT and 26 ASP. 1 week following procedure, re-thrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) CDT and 6 (23.1%) ASP (p<0.5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8%) ASP case. Composite of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Prior to PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) CDT and 8 (30.8%) ASP (p<0.05). PTC mild in 13 (46.4%) CDT and 5 (19.2%) ASP (p<0.05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) CDT and 5 (19.2%) ASP, severe in 9 (32.1%) CDT and 8 (30.8) ASP. At early follow up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) CDT and 4 (23.5) ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) CDT and 1 (5.9%) ASP, severe in 9(39.1%) CDT and 6 (35.3%) ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) CDT and 6 (35%) ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency of 22 (95%) CDT and 15 (88%) ASP. CONCLUSION: ASP and CDT may both be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS, however, they differ on early efficacy, PTC, and patency. While often more rapid and convenient, our results suggest ASP may be inferior to CAT in management of PSS.

title: Multicenter Outcomes of Peripheral Vascular Interventions in Patients with Active Cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cancer is typically associated with venous thrombosis, but its impact on patients undergoing peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) for concomitant peripheral arterial disease (PAD) remains unclear. This multicenter study examines the characteristics of patients with active cancer and their outcomes after PVI. METHODS: Institutional vascular quality initiative (VQI) PVI data from 3 tertiary care centers (2019-2023) were combined and expanded through a retrospective chart review to include the presence and types of cancer. All adult patients undergoing endovascular intervention for PAD, including those with claudication, chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and acute limb ischemia (ALI), were included. The primary outcome was the composite of major amputation or mortality at 4 years in patients with cancer compared to those without. Additional long-term outcomes included reintervention, mortality, and major amputation at both 1 and 4 years. Secondary outcomes included perioperative outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 3,072 patients were included. The incidence of active cancer was 2.2% (N=68). Lung cancer was the most common, affecting 30.9% (N=21) of patients. 53% (N=36) presented with advanced stages (3/4) irrespective of cancer type. Patients with cancer were less likely to have diabetes. There was no significant difference in indication, but patients with cancer were more likely to get treated for aortoiliac disease and undergo stenting. Patients with cancer had a higher incidence of distal embolization (4.4% vs 0.6%, P=0.012) and perioperative major amputation (4.4% vs 1.3%, P=0.046). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly higher mortality or amputation in patients with cancer up to 4 years (63% vs 35.1%, P<0.001). Late outcomes in patients with cancer were driven by significantly higher mortality (52.2% vs. 28.3%, p<.001) rather than adverse limb events (amputation: 14.7% vs. 11.4%, p=.50; reintervention:47.8% vs. 48.3%, p=.80). Regression analysis demonstrated independent association of cancer with the composite outcome of mortality or major amputation (aHR=2.24 [1.61-3.10]). CONCLUSION: Active cancer affects a small proportion of patients undergoing PVI but has a significant impact on perioperative limb outcomes and long-term survival. This multicenter collaboration, combining registry data and EMR review, can shed light on less common risk factors affecting lower extremity revascularization.

title: Outcomes among Patients with Single-Vessel Tibial Runoff Undergoing Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia, and the Role of Peroneal Communicating Branch Quality.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, Peroneal Communicating Branch (PCB) Grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB Grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB Grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB Grade 3), and compared each to the single-vessel AT/PT reference group. RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted two-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group (19% vs. 9.4% [AT] vs. 8.7% [PT]; P<.001), as were MALE rates (30% vs. 14% vs. 26%; P=.01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation (HR 1.81 [1.04-3.13]) and MALE (HR 1.52 [1.03-2.25]) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR 2.09 [1.06-4.13]; MALE: HR 1.59 [1.08-2.35]) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB Grades, unadjusted one-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern (6.9% (AT/PT) vs. 5.4% (PCB Grade 1) vs. 15% (PCB Grade 2) vs. 32% (PCB Grade 3); P<.001). After adjustment, when compared to AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB Grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR 3.21 [1.76-4.84]) and MALE (HR 2.41 [1.53-3.79]), while those with two branches with at least one being robust (PCB Grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR 1.69 [1.09-2.62]) and no difference in major amputation or MALE. CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Those with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable to AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and pre-operative assessment of peroneal communicating branch quality - using the proposed PCB Grading system - in revascularization planning.

title: Faculty Narrative Feedback in the Vascular Surgery Entrustable Professional Activity (EPA) Pilot is Disproportionately Focused on Patient Care and Medical Knowledge Competencies.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of Entrustable Professional Activities (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. ACGME Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity. It is unclear how faculty use this information to guide and focus the content of their feedback. We sought to identify the core competencies reflected in narrative feedback in a multi-institutional study of EPA assessments. METHODS: EPA assessments were collected during a 3-month national Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. Trainees were rated on their performance of EPAs on a 4-point Likert scale and faculty had the opportunity to provide feedback. Narrative feedback was qualitatively analyzed using focused coding guided by the Vascular Surgery Milestones 2.0 framework. Feedback was coded using the six ACGME Core Competencies-patient care (PC), medical knowledge (MK), professionalism (PROF), interpersonal and communication skills (ICS), practice-based learning and improvement (PBLI), and systems-based practice (SBP)-to characterize the domains emphasized in feedback. Quality assessment scores were assigned to all narrative feedback using the Quality of Assessment of Learning (QuAL) framework. Descriptive analysis was completed using R. RESULTS: Faculty completed 983 EPA assessments of 78 trainees across 17 institutions (n=16 integrated residencies, n=12 fellowships). Narrative feedback was included in 760 (77%) assessments. Feedback most frequently addressed PC (n=662, 82%), followed by MK (n=418, 55%), while feedback about PBLI (n=42, 6%), ICS (n =42,6%), PROF (n=20, 3%), and SBP (n=26, 3%) were less common. Most assessments were completed for PGY-3 (29%) and PGY-4 trainees (22%). Most assessments occurred during the intra-operative phase of care (88%), with relatively few occurring in pre-operative (7%) or post-operative (5%) phases. Additionally, feedback referencing PC was associated with higher odds of high-quality feedback in comparison to feedback about the other competencies (OR = 25.56, 95% CI: 6.13-106.55). CONCLUSION: In this multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, faculty most frequently provided trainees with feedback on their performance of PC and MK competencies. Feedback on performance related to SBP was infrequently provided and, when provided, was of generally low quality. This has important implications for the use of EPAs to inform ACGME Milestones ratings and suggests alternative assessment tools will continue to be needed to capture performance across all competency domains required of a physician.

title: Endovascular stenting of extracranial cervical artery dissections: A two-center study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Extracranial arterial dissections (EAD) are uncommon in the general population but represent a relatively frequent cause of ischemic stroke in young adults. Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-four EAD patients who underwent stenting were included. A standardized follow-up protocol at 12 months consisting of a clinical neurological assessment accompanied by imaging studies, including either Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Digital Subtraction Angiography was adopted. RESULTS: In our cohort, most dissections were spontaneous (81 %) and predominantly involved the internal carotid artery (85 %), with acute stroke being the most common indication for stenting. Technical success was achieved in 85.7 % and complications occurred in 10 %. Three patients with initial stent implantation failure underwent successful secondary attempt. No significant predictors of technical success were identified. At discharge, good functional outcome was observed in 83 % of patients and at 12 months most followed patients showed favorable radiological results with high stent patency (86 %) and excellent clinical outcomes (mRS 0-2 in 97 %). CONCLUSION: The results of our study suggest that for selected patients with medical therapy failure or hemodynamic compromise, stenting is a reasonable alternative. Given the limited evidence on indications, safety and efficacy, further randomized studies comparing stenting with medical management are warranted.
